rfp_analysis.detected_priority_note: The RFP rules out a database migration and asks for rollout with minimal disruption. Proposals that change NordFrame’s infrastructure should lose points.

requirements.text: A web-based dashboard showing real-time inventory levels across all 6 warehouses.
Alerts to warehouse managers when items fall below a configurable threshold.
Integration with the existing PostgreSQL inventory database, with no migration to a new database.
requirements.source_quote: no migration to a new database

requirements.text: Warehouse managers see only their own site; HQ staff see all sites.
A data migration / onboarding plan for all 6 sites with minimal disruption.
Support and maintenance terms after go-live, including response times and SLAs.
Clear documentation of assumptions, limitations or risks, since inventory decisions will rely on the system.
€80,000–€120,000 total, including the first year of support.
requirements.source_quote: €80,000–€120,000 total, including first year of support

requirements.text: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months; all 6 sites within 6 months.
requirements.source_quote: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months

scoring.verdict: Pricing and timeline are both deferred, four of the seven RFP requirements are never mentioned, and nothing ties the proposal to NordFrame’s situation.

criteria.name: Completeness vs RFP Requirements
criteria.comment: Requirements 3, 5, 6 and 7 are not mentioned; 1, 2 and 4 are only touched on in a phrase each.

criteria.name: Risk/Assumptions Transparency
criteria.comment: No assumptions, dependencies or risks anywhere, although the RFP asks for them explicitly.

criteria.name: Pricing Clarity
criteria.comment: No figure at all, although the client published a €80,000–€120,000 budget.
citations: Pricing will be provided upon further discussion
€80,000–€120,000 total, including first year of support

criteria.name: Timeline Clarity
criteria.comment: No dates or milestones against the 3-month pilot and 6-month rollout the RFP sets.
citations: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months

criteria.name: Data Accuracy & Validation
criteria.comment: Nothing about checking the figures: no validation step, no parallel run against the current spreadsheets, no mention of who confirms the data is right.

criteria.name: Problem Understanding
criteria.comment: Restates the need for “better visibility” but never mentions the 6 sites, Germany and Austria, or the spreadsheet and legacy setup the RFP describes.
citations: NordFrame needs better visibility into warehouse inventory
6 regional warehouses across Germany and Austria

criteria.name: Scope & Deliverables Clarity
criteria.comment: Three one-line features with no detail: no site count, no alert thresholds or recipients, no user roles, and nothing about what is out of scope.

criteria.name: Tone & Persuasiveness
criteria.comment: Generic claims (“modern, scalable cloud architecture”, “talented team”) with no NordFrame-specific evidence or references.
citations: modern, scalable cloud architecture and industry best practices

criteria.name: Legacy System & Spreadsheets
criteria.comment: The legacy system and the spreadsheets are never mentioned, so it is unclear whether NordFrame would end up running two systems.

findings.reason: Promises a “cloud-based dashboard” with real-time data but never says it covers all 6 warehouses or runs in the browser.
findings.citation: cloud-based dashboard that displays inventory data in real time
findings.suggested_patch: In “Our Approach”, replace the first sentence with: “We will build a web-based dashboard that shows live stock levels for all 6 NordFrame warehouses in Germany and Austria on one screen, with a drill-down per site.”

findings.reason: Lists “Notifications for low stock” but not who receives them or that thresholds can be configured.
findings.suggested_patch: Expand the bullet to: “Low-stock alerts: each warehouse manager is notified automatically when an item falls below a threshold that can be set per item.”

findings.reason: PostgreSQL is never mentioned. “Cloud-based” leaves open whether NordFrame’s data would be moved, which the RFP rules out.
findings.suggested_patch: Add to “Our Approach”: “The dashboard connects to NordFrame’s existing PostgreSQL inventory database. No data is migrated and no new database is introduced.”

findings.reason: “Secure login for different users” doesn’t state the site-level rule the RFP sets.
findings.suggested_patch: Replace the bullet with: “Role-based access: warehouse managers see only their own site; HQ staff see all 6 sites.”

findings.reason: No rollout or onboarding plan for the 6 sites.
findings.suggested_patch: Add a “Rollout plan” section: which warehouse pilots first, the order the other 5 follow, and how each site keeps working (for example, running spreadsheets in parallel) until the data is confirmed.

findings.reason: No support or maintenance terms after go-live.
findings.suggested_patch: Add a “Support & maintenance” section with response times per severity (critical, minor), support hours, and what Year 1 support includes.

findings.reason: No assumptions, limitations or risks, which the RFP explicitly requests.
findings.suggested_patch: Add a “Risks & assumptions” section naming real dependencies, such as read access to the PostgreSQL database and a contact person at each warehouse, and what happens to the schedule if they slip.

findings.reason: Pricing is deferred “upon further discussion” although the client published a budget.
findings.citation: Pricing will be provided upon further discussion
findings.suggested_patch: Replace the Pricing section with an itemised estimate inside €80,000–€120,000 (dashboard, alerts and access, rollout, Year 1 support), and say which items could change after discovery.

findings.reason: “In a timely manner” gives no dates against a 3-month pilot and a 6-month rollout.
findings.suggested_patch: Add a milestone table: pilot live at one warehouse by Month 3, remaining 5 sites by Month 6, with the checkpoints in between.
